title: Raleigh's Holiday Season Without a Holiday Express Ticket
summary: Pullen Park's Holiday Express sold out in October. The tree lightings, the parade and the arboretum's last Moonlight nights all happen Nov. 20–21. Here are times, prices and parking tips.
body_markdown:
On October 15 at 9 a.m., the City of Raleigh opened Ticketmaster sales for the 2026 Pullen Park Holiday Express. By November 10, the[City's Holiday Express page](https://raleighnc.gov/parks-and-recreation/services/holiday-express) had a sold-out notice at the top. That fits the event's history.[WRAL](https://www.wral.com/lifestyles/pullen-park-holiday-express-presented-by-wral-tickets-on-sale-october-2026/) has reported that Holiday Express usually sells out within a few hours.


The rest of Raleigh's holiday calendar works the other way. Most of it falls on the two days right after this post goes up, Friday, Nov. 20 and Saturday, Nov. 21, and most of those events are free. Two tree lightings, the Christmas parade, an adults-only night at Pullen Park and the last nights of the arboretum's garden lights all happen within about 27 hours, and a household without a Holiday Express ticket can still fill both days.


## Friday night starts at Moore Square


The Downtown Raleigh Alliance holds its 18th annual[Raleigh Tree Lighting and Holiday Market](https://downtownraleigh.org/dra-programs/tree-lighting) at Moore Square on Friday, Nov. 20, from 5:30 to 8 p.m. It is free and open to the public.[ABC11's 2026 holiday guide](https://abc11.com/post/nc-holiday-guide-2026-christmas-parades-events-light-displays-central/20033841) also lists free Santa photos.


The Alliance's lineup reads like a downtown weeknight with a tree added. About 25 local makers and artisans run the market. Sidecar Social Club, Ladies in Red and the Moore Square Middle Honors Chorus perform. Children can write letters to Santa, make ornaments or get Fairy Hair. Food comes from Curry in a Hurry, Bare Baked Pizza, Shawarma Bowl, Hollywood Taco and The Kupkake Shoppe, and Lucky Tree has coffee and warm drinks. Crank Arm Brewing, Wye Hill, Element and Raleigh Wine Shop pour the beer and wine. You can get dinner from the food list alone and still be home early. That matters, because Saturday starts early.


Friday is also the first night of the final weekend of Moonlight in the Garden at the JC Raulston Arboretum. More on that below, since it's Saturday's best evening option too.


## Saturday morning belongs to the parade


The[82nd Raleigh Christmas Parade](https://grma.org/christmas-parade/) steps off at 9:30 a.m. on Saturday, Nov. 21. The Greater Raleigh Merchants Association bills it as the largest Christmas parade between Washington, D.C. and Atlanta. NC State Chancellor Kevin Howell is the 2026 grand marshal.[ABC11's parade preview](https://abc11.com/post/raleigh-christmas-parade-bring-merry-cheer-downtown-most-wonderful-time-year/20026463/) counts 115 entries this year, and the station's holiday guide lists the parade as free.


The route is about 1.4 miles. It starts at Hillsborough and St. Mary's Streets, heads east to the Capitol, follows Salisbury, Morgan and Fayetteville Streets, and disbands at Lenoir Street.[Visit Raleigh's parade guide](https://www.visitraleigh.com/plan-a-trip/visitraleigh-insider-blog/post/a-guide-to-the-raleigh-christmas-parade/) expects it to end around noon and says ABC11 will broadcast live from 9:30.


Visit Raleigh's practical advice is to arrive by 8:30 a.m. or earlier if you want a front-row spot at the curb, which is first-come, first-served. City-owned parking decks are free on parade morning, and downtown street parking is free on weekends. The Alexander Square deck at 230 S. Wilmington St. has elevated views of the route but can fill early. Fayetteville Street is near the end of the route, so a spot near Lenoir gets the parade last and lets you walk out quickly once it disbands.


## Saturday afternoon moves to North Hills


The afternoon is free.[Christmas at North Hills](https://www.visitnorthhills.com/signature-events/christmas-at-north-hills-series) holds its tree lighting at North Hills Commons on Saturday from 4 to 7 p.m. It has live entertainment, children's crafts and a vendor village, and the 41-foot tree is lit when Santa arrives. Visit Raleigh's 2026 listing gives the address as 4191 Main at North Hills St. and says admission is free.


Moore Square is the downtown version of this event, and North Hills is the Midtown version. Both happen on the same weekend, so one household can go to both: Friday downtown, Saturday in Midtown.


## Saturday night has two ticketed choices


After dark, both evening options are ticketed. Pullen Park's sells through RecLink, and the arboretum's sells timed entries ahead, with gate tickets only if any are left.


**Pullen Park After Dark: Merry & Bright.** This adults-only night at Pullen Park runs from 6:30 to 9 p.m. on Saturday. Tickets are $20 and went on sale October 2 through RecLink. For adults without a Holiday Express ticket, this is the other way to see Pullen Park lit for the season.


**Moonlight in the Garden.** The JC Raulston Arboretum, at 4415 Beryl Road, ends its three-weekend run on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 20 and 21. It has lit gardens, live music, food trucks, fire pits and hot apple cider. The[arboretum's Moonlight page](https://jcra.ncsu.edu/moonlight/) calls it the arboretum's largest annual fundraiser, the one that keeps daytime admission free all year. Advance tickets are timed, with entry slots from 5:30 to 8 p.m. They cost $30 for general admission, $20 for arboretum members and college students, and $5 for children 12 and under. If gate tickets are still available, they cost $40 for adults and $5 for children. Some time slots have already sold out, so buying ahead is cheaper and more certain.

Fri., Nov. 20, 5:30–8 p.m. entries Moonlight in the Garden JC Raulston Arboretum $30 advance, $5 kids


Sat., Nov. 21, 9:30 a.m. to about noon Raleigh Christmas Parade Hillsborough St. to Fayetteville St. Free

Sat., Nov. 21, 6:30–9 p.m. Pullen Park After Dark: Merry & Bright Pullen Park $20, adults only


## December is quieter, and two dates need planning


After Thanksgiving there are fewer events, and each one takes a little more planning.


Holiday Express opens at Pullen Park on Tuesday, Dec. 1 and runs nightly into mid-December, from 5 to 9:30 p.m. Tickets were $21 plus tax and fees, and everyone age one and older needs one, including guests who won't ride the train. Ticket holders should bring the digital ticket on their phone, since the City does not accept screenshots or printouts at the entrance. Inside, the ticket covers every activity except café snacks and souvenirs, and the ticketed train time is fixed. This year adds the Club Cocoa Lounge, a paid hot-chocolate bar in Shelter 1 run by Pullen Café. Sensory-friendly sessions run Dec. 6 and Dec. 13 from 1 to 4 p.m., with lower music volume and smaller crowds.


The free December event to put on the calendar now is the North Carolina Museum of Art's[Winter Lantern Walk](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/winter-lantern-walk/) on Saturday, Dec. 12, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. at the Museum Park Ellipse. Walkers bring their own homemade lanterns, and the lanterns can't use flame. The procession lines up at 5:30 p.m. and follows a three-quarter-mile paved loop. Registration is required and space is limited. Of all the December events, this is the closest to Holiday Express in how it works: it costs nothing, but you have to sign up ahead.


Downtown, the City's[Raleigh for the Holidays page](https://raleighnc.gov/holidays) lists the Downtown Raleigh Alliance's Illuminate Art Walk from Dec. 4 through Jan. 3. Its run extends past New Year's, after every other event on this list has ended.


For more on the restaurants and districts near these events, see our earlier[guide to what's new in Raleigh](https://spotlightnc.com/blog/whats-new-in-raleigh-this-august-openings-markets-and-nights-worth-leaving-the-house-for) and our[Raleigh neighborhood page](https://spotlightnc.com/neighborhoods/raleigh) .


If you're planning holiday weekends around this calendar and wondering which parts of Raleigh put Moore Square, North Hills or Pullen Park within an easy drive or walk,[Spotlight Realty](https://spotlightnc.com/) is glad to talk it through. We're happy to share what we know whenever it's useful to you.
